event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: ED’s 2021-02-18 filing discusses COVID-19 as an active and evolving threat only 11 months after the WHO declaration, so no time-decay discount applies.  The narrative spans actual, quantified hits (e.g., $61 million in foregone revenue), operational stresses (remote-work cyber exposure, supply-chain vigilance, suspended collections), and forward-looking uncertainty over liquidity and demand.  Language is mostly specific—linking the pandemic to lower billed sales, higher uncollectibles, slower cash recovery and potential increases in bad-debt expense—yet it also notes partial offsets such as revenue-decoupling mechanisms.  Because the disclosures combine realised financial pain with continuing, not-fully-quantifiable exposures, overall risk is assessed as elevated but not catastrophic: high severity, medium-high likelihood, tempered by some structural mitigants.

evidence_list.snippet: There has been a growing use of COVID-19 related themes by malicious cyber actors and the significant increase in employees working remotely has increased the attack surface area for the Companies as well as their contractors and vendors .

components.reason: Directly ties COVID-19 to increased cyber-security risk.
Highlights specific operational driver (remote work) that widens risk surface.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Links pandemic-induced remote work to an expanded cyber-attack surface, a concrete operational vulnerability.

evidence_list.snippet: The Companies Face Risks Related To Health Epidemics And Other Outbreaks, Including The COVID-19 Pandemic.

components.reason: Explicit identification of COVID-19 as a corporate risk category.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but clear acknowledgement that COVID-19 constitutes a risk.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has impacted, and continues to impact, countries, communities, supply chains and markets.

components.reason: States ongoing, wide-ranging impact on supply chains and markets.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad statement of continuing impacts across supply chains and markets.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, there has been an economic slowdown in the Companies’ service territories, decreased demand for the services that they provide and changes in governmental and regulatory policy.

components.reason: Connects pandemic to economic slowdown and decreased demand—direct revenue pressure.
Specifies geography (company service territories) and regulatory change.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Details demand contraction and policy shifts tied directly to COVID-19.

evidence_list.snippet: The decline in business activity in the Companies’ service territories has resulted in lower billed sales revenues and increased difficulty of customers to pay bills.

components.reason: Describes realised financial impacts: lower revenues and payment difficulty.
Cites customer-level stress affecting cash collection.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows concrete, already-experienced revenue and cash-collection hits.

evidence_list.snippet: Although the Utilities’ New York electric and gas businesses have largely effective revenue decoupling mechanisms in place, lower billed sales revenues and higher uncollectible accounts have impacted and could continue to impact the Companies’ liquidity.

components.reason: States present and future liquidity impact from reduced sales and higher bad debt.
Includes mitigating factor (revenue-decoupling mechanisms).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Liquidity risk identified but partially offset by existing rate mechanisms.

evidence_list.snippet: The Utilities have also suspended service disconnections, new late payment charges and certain other fees for customers, which may result in a further increase to bad debt expense.

components.reason: Links operational policy change due to COVID-19 to higher bad-debt risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Explains how pandemic-driven customer relief could elevate credit losses.

evidence_list.snippet: The Companies will continue to monitor developments relating to the COVID-19 pandemic; however, the Companies cannot predict the extent to which, COVID-19 may have a material impact on liquidity, financial condition, and results of operations.

components.reason: Acknowledges uncertainty and potential material impact on core financial metrics.
Expresses inability to quantify, signalling risk but with vagueness.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights material uncertainty but lacks specifics, so modest score.

evidence_list.snippet: During 2020, the decline in business activity in the Utilities’ service territory as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic resulted in lower billed sales revenues in 2020 and a slower recovery in cash of outstanding customer accounts receivable balances and is expected to continue to do so in 2021.

components.reason: Reports realised revenue and cash-flow degradation.
Provides forward-looking expectation of continuation into 2021.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Actual 2020 hit with explicit expectation of ongoing pressure earns high score.

evidence_list.snippet: Although these revenue decoupling mechanisms are in place, lower billed sales revenues and higher uncollectible accounts have reduced and is expected to continue to reduce liquidity at the Utilities.

components.reason: Specifies liquidity reduction linked to COVID-19 revenue effects.
Notes mitigating decoupling mechanisms.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Liquidity strain discussed, but partially cushioned by mechanisms.

evidence_list.snippet: Also, in March 2020, the Utilities began suspending service disconnections, certain collection notices, final bill collection agency activity, new late payment charges and certain other fees for all customers and such suspensions may continue through 2021 or later.

components.reason: Describes ongoing customer-relief measures that prolong revenue pressure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Extended suspension of collections points to sustained cash-flow risk.

evidence_list.snippet: For the year ended December 31, 2020, the estimated foregone revenues that were not collected by the Utilities were approximately $61 million for CECONY and $3 million for O&R.

components.reason: Provides concrete, quantified financial impact directly attributable to pandemic policies.
Material magnitude (eight-figure hit) across two utilities.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Quantified $64 million revenue loss is strong evidence of material impact.

evidence_list.snippet: The Companies have procured an inventory of pandemic-related materials to address anticipated future needs and maintain regular communications with key suppliers.

components.reason: Shows proactive mitigation of supply-chain risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Purely mitigative; does not elevate risk score, so nets to zero.
